Fleet flight dynamics validation

12 October 2026 · local implementation · no publication

All four aircraft now share force-based aerodynamics and rigid-body rotation. The former jet acceleration shortcuts and direct attitude-rate integration were replaced. The beginner controller commands rate-limited control surfaces; it adds no free lift or thrust.

Implemented model

  • Measured main-wing area, span and mean chord. Attached-flow lift intercept/slope fit to the private tester’s 96-panel solution at 0° and 4°.
  • Declared component budgets for airframe, engines, gear, tail, equipment, payload and fuel. CG is mass-weighted; full cuboid and parallel-axis inertia tensors update with fuel loading.
  • ISA density, lift, induced/profile/configuration drag, sideslip, continuous post-stall estimates, estimated stability/damping/control moments, thrust-line moments and CG displacement.
  • Rotational equation I·omegaDot = moment − omega×(I·omega), midpoint quaternion integration, and center-of-mass translation with the render datum recovered from CG.
  • Bounded shaft-power propeller thrust, estimated installed jet maps, engine spool, fuel use, flap and gear actuation. Ground support moments prevent power-only rotation; touchdown requires deployed gear.
  • The same physical actuator positions drive visible flight-control, flap and gear animations. Flight hints use aircraft-specific speeds.

Departure and landing checks

Sea-level nominal loading, Palm Bay’s existing 470 m runway, default wind, assisted departure and a controlled 20-second approach/stop exercise. Climb inputs remain inside the estimated AOA envelope. Speeds are true airspeeds in knots.

Aurelia’s conceptual installation is sized at two 25 kN engines against its measured wing, 5.66 t loading and Palm Bay departure. This replaces an undersized initial 38 kN estimate. It is an explicit original-design assumption, not a manufacturer rating. Aircraft-specific pitch limits preserve the default departure’s terrain clearance without changing gravity, weight or airfield geometry.

Unassisted trim across loading and density

32 conditions: four fuel/payload combinations and two altitudes per aircraft. The trim solver balances longitudinal force and pitch moment within 10⁻⁶ N and N·m. The actual simulation then runs for 20 seconds with assistance disabled and constant zero wind; altitude drift must stay below 1 m and speed drift below 0.2 m/s. Fuel consumption remains enabled.

Verification

177 tests and 74,159 assertions passed. Main game and private tester production builds passed. Tests cover mass response, CG limits, tensor inversion, angular momentum/energy, force/control signs, geometric lift fit, trim, actuator limits, fuel, natural stall recovery, runway contact, takeoff, touchdown, and 30/60/120 Hz consistency.

Four real keyboard departures and four deterministic seeded landings passed in the actual browser game, with zero page/console errors. Rendered gear and control surfaces matched the physical state. The approach checks are seeded simulations, not complete human-flown landing sequences.

Model validity

These are original concept aircraft with numerically verified behavior. Component densities/envelopes, CLmax/post-stall behavior, viscous drag, tail/stability derivatives, neutral points, engine maps and fuel rates remain engineering estimates. The main-wing vortex solution excludes fuselage, tail interference, viscosity, stall and chamber-wall effects. It is not full-aircraft CFD or measured validation.

Ground contact for Finch and the two legacy jet rigs remains an approximation; Stormbird uses the authored tire profiles and measured body hull. Tire/structure loads, flutter, detailed swept-volume clearance, icing, transonic/supersonic flow and certification are outside these checks. Estimated drag rise does not validate high-Mach performance. Strong gusts, extreme loading and inverted/post-stall flight require a broader flight-test envelope.

Repeatable workflow

bun scripts/validate-fleet-dynamics.ts --browser runs the test suite, both builds, the live local browser checks and this matrix. Start the game locally on port 5175 first; FLIGHT_CHECK_URL selects another local server. A geometry change that disagrees with the private solver fails the regression rather than silently keeping stale lift curves.

References

Project aircraft handbook; NASA lift equation; NASA drag equation; NASA force and torque trim; JSBSim mass and inertia conventions.
